references.text: God's promise to Abraham to make his descendants a great nation, which Moses reminds God of in his intercession.
God promises Abraham that his descendants will be as numerous as the stars in the sky and that they will inherit the land.
God's eternal covenant with Abraham and the promise of the land of Canaan to his descendants as an everlasting possession.
God swears by Himself to Abraham and promises to multiply his offspring like the stars in the sky.
God confirms the promise to Isaac regarding the land and descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, because of His oath to Abraham.
God repeats the promise to Jacob (Israel) concerning the land and that his offspring will be like the dust of the earth.
Jacob reminds God of the promise to make his offspring as numerous as the sand on the seashore.
God confirms the promise to Jacob that nations will come from him and that the land will be given to his descendants.
Moses refers to the same intercession where he asks God to remember His servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God shows Moses the land He swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and their descendants.
A reference to the fact that God swore by Himself when giving the promise to Abraham, since there is no one greater to swear by.
Paul speaks of the Israelites who received the covenants and promises and who descend from the fathers.
God's eternal oath to the fathers serves as the theological foundation both for the exodus from Egypt and for Moses' prayer to turn away God's wrath.
The same oath that Moses uses in prayer to stop judgment is used as the basis for the command to the people to take possession of the land.
The direct gift of the land to Jacob in Genesis is referred to in Exodus 32 as an unshakable promise which Moses appeals to.
Moses explicitly cites the specific prophecy of Isaac about 'the stars in the sky' to remind God of His own oath.
The NT text expands the content of the same covenant from the gift of land to a universal blessing for all nations through Abraham's offspring.
The verses form a direct dialogue in the narrative where Moses uses the content of the oath (32:13) and God confirms that He will fulfill it (33:1).
Jacob's retelling of the promise of 'eternal possession' in Genesis strengthens Moses' argument about God's unbreakable oath in Exodus.
The prophecy in Ezekiel builds directly on the same oath that Moses appealed to, confirming that the promise of the land stands firm through the exile.
The individual promise made to Isaac in Genesis becomes in Exodus 32 the collective basis for God's grace toward the entire nation.
